scenario.name: incident_5_v2
scenario.title: Spearphishing Attachment → Process Injection → LSASS Dump → Domain Discovery → Lateral Movement
scenario.description:
Endpoint-focused intrusion where a threat actor delivers a malicious document via
spearphishing email. Upon execution, the payload injects into a legitimate system
process to evade endpoint detection, then dumps LSASS memory to harvest domain
credentials. The attacker enumerates domain accounts to identify high-value targets
before using stolen credentials to move laterally to a secondary workstation via
SMB/Windows Admin Shares.
scenario.entry_point: Spearphishing attachment delivered via email to victim workstation
scenario.final_objective: Lateral movement to secondary workstation using harvested domain credentials

attack_paths.description:
A threat actor crafts a weaponized Office document (.docm with embedded macro) and
delivers it via spearphishing email targeting jsmith at CONTOSO.LOCAL. The email
mimics a legitimate business communication (invoice notification) and arrives at
the victim's mailbox on wkst-victim. This is visible in OfficeActivity logs as an
email receive event with attachment metadata.

Upon opening the attachment, the embedded macro executes a PowerShell stager that
establishes an initial shell (INITIAL_SHELL) on the victim workstation. The process
chain WINWORD.EXE → powershell.exe → cmd.exe is captured in DeviceProcessEvents
with full command-line arguments. SysmonEvents EID 1 also records process creation.

The malware immediately performs process injection (T1055) into svchost.exe, a
legitimate Windows system process, using CreateRemoteThread. This grants the
attacker SYSTEM-level execution context (SYSTEM_ACCESS) while evading EDR tooling
that monitors user-space processes. SysmonEvents EID 8 captures the cross-process
thread creation, and DeviceProcessEvents records the anomalous memory operations.
The mdatp-engine generates an AlertInfo record for suspicious process injection.

Operating from the injected process with elevated privileges, the attacker dumps
LSASS process memory (T1003.001) using an in-memory reflective technique (no
procdump.exe on disk). The memory dump yields NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets for
domain accounts, including dadmin's domain admin credentials (DOMAIN_CREDENTIALS).
DeviceProcessEvents logs the LSASS handle access, WindowsSecurityEvents records
event 4656 (handle request to lsass.exe) and 4663 (object access), and AlertInfo
captures the credential theft alert.

With domain credentials, the attacker performs LDAP reconnaissance against dc01
(T1087.002), querying the domain controller for members of Domain Admins, Enterprise
Admins, and other privileged groups. WindowsSecurityEvents event 4662 on the DC logs
the directory service access. This confirms dadmin has admin access to wkst-target.

mitigations.description: Train users to identify malicious attachments and report them quickly.
Block execution of mounted ISO contents and unsigned executables from email.
Detonate inbound attachments in a sandbox; block ISO / LNK / HTA where possible.
